attributes.description: <<-EOT    ACCOUNT analyses this account only. ORGANIZATION analyses every account in    the organization and must be created in the delegated administrator account    (or the management account), not in a member account.  EOT
Name of the unused-access analyzer.

<<-EOT    Days of non-use after which a permission, role, user or key is reported.    AWS accepts 1 to 365. 90 is the usual first target; going below 45 produces    findings for anything with a quarterly or seasonal usage pattern.  EOT
Account IDs whose IAM entities are not analysed (e.g. a sandbox OU). Every exclusion is a blind spot: list them in the ticket that asked for them.
IAM entities carrying any of these tag sets are not analysed, e.g. [{ "access-analyzer-exempt" = "break-glass" }].
Tags applied to the analyzer.
ARN of the unused-access analyzer.
Resolved analyzer type, e.g. ORGANIZATION_UNUSED_ACCESS.
Maximum session length in seconds. Keep it close to the longest job.
Managed policy ARNs attached to the role.
Optional permissions boundary for the role.
Create the token.actions.githubusercontent.com provider. Set false if it already exists in the account (only one per account is allowed).
Tags applied to created resources.

<<-EOT    Exact `sub` claim values allowed to assume the role. Prefer environment    subjects (repo:ORG/REPO:environment:production) so that GitHub environment    protection rules gate access. Repositories created after 2026-07-15, or    that opted in, use the immutable format repo:ORG@ORG_ID/REPO@REPO_ID:...  EOT
Name of the IAM role GitHub Actions will assume.
Pass to aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials as role-to-assume.
Rendered trust policy, for review.
Role assignments for the identity: list of { scope, role_definition_name }.
Tags applied to the identity.

<<-EOT    Map of credential name => exact GitHub `sub` claim. Entra ID matches the    subject literally (no wildcards), and an identity holds at most 20    federated credentials. Example:      { prod = "repo:my-org/my-repo:environment:production" }  EOT
Azure region of the identity.
Name of the user-assigned managed identity used by the workflow.
Object ID of the identity, for additional role assignments.
Pass to azure/login as client-id (with tenant-id and subscription-id).
Resource group that holds the identity.
Workload identity pool ID.
Account ID (the part before @) of the service account the workflow impersonates.
Exact GitHub `sub` values allowed to impersonate the service account, e.g. repo:my-org/my-repo:environment:production. google.subject is limited to 127 bytes.
Numeric GitHub organization/user ID (repository_owner_id claim). IDs are never reassigned; names can be re-registered after deletion.
Numeric project number (principal identifiers use the number, not the ID).
Pass to google-github-actions/auth as service_account.
Pass to google-github-actions/auth as workload_identity_provider.
Project that hosts the workload identity pool and the service account.
Tags applied to every resource this module creates.
ARN of the created bucket.
Name of the S3 bucket used by this example app.
AWS region for the provider and the resources it manages.
Name of the example S3 bucket.
